## Summary
Implement automatic creation of required Ralph GitHub labels (`ralph:ready`, `ralph:in-progress`, `ralph:done`, etc.) when the daemon starts managing a new repository. This prevents runtime failures when attempting to claim issues in repos without pre-configured labels.

## Problem
Currently, the daemon fails to claim issues when required labels don't exist in the repository:
```
warning: failed to claim issue #1: orchestration error: gh issue edit (claim) failed for owner/repo#1: 'ralph:in-progress' not found
```

## Requirements
- Automatically create all required Ralph labels during the `clone_or_bootstrap` phase or at the start of each repo's runtime
- Use `gh label create` command (idempotent operation — skip if label already exists)
- Required labels to create:
  - `ralph:ready`
  - `ralph:in-progress`
  - `ralph:done`
  - (any other labels used by the daemon workflow)
- Handle errors gracefully (log warnings but don't fail bootstrap if label creation fails)

## Implementation Location
- Primary file: `src/daemon/bootstrap.rs`
- May involve: `src/backend/gh.rs` or label-related utilities

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Labels are created automatically during repo bootstrap/initialization
- [ ] Operation is idempotent (doesn't error if labels already exist)
- [ ] All required Ralph labels are included in the creation list
- [ ] Daemon can successfully claim issues on freshly-cloned repos without manual label setup
- [ ] Appropriate error handling and logging for label creation failures
